author: alexcrichton
body:
The `library/std/src/sys_common/net.rs` module is intended to define common implementations of networking-related APIs across a variety of platforms that share similar APIs (e.g. Berkeley-style sockets and all). This module is not included for more fringe targets however such as UEFI or "unknown" targets to libstd (those classified as `restricted-std`). Previously the `sys_common/net.rs` file was set up such that an allow-list indicated it shouldn't be used. This commit inverts the logic to have an allow-list of when it should be used instead.

The goal of this commit is to make it a bit easier to experiment with a new Rust target. Currently more esoteric targets are required to get an exception in this `cfg_if` block to use `crate::sys::net` such as for unsupported targets. With this inversion of logic only targets which actually support networking will be listed, where most of those are lumped under `cfg(unix)`.

Given that this change is likely to cause some breakage for some target by accident I've attempted to be somewhat robust with this by following these steps to defining the new predicate for inverted logic.

1. Take all supported targets and filter out all `cfg(unix)` ones as these should all support `sys_common/net.rs`.
2. Take remaining targets and filter out `cfg(windows)` ones.
3. The remaining dozen-or-so targets were all audited by hand. Mostly this included `target_os = "hermit"` and `target_os = "solid_asp3"` which required an allow-list entry, but remaining targets were all already excluded (didn't use `sys_common/net.rs` so they were left out.

If this causes breakage it should be relatively easy to fix and I'd be happy to follow-up with any PRs necessary.

I've implemented a free (CC BY 4.0) cbrt algorithm for floats (Moroz L, Samotyy V, Walczyk CJ, Cieśliński JL.). Cube roots are required for many color space conversions, so in my opinion, this is an important feature for a standard library. I personally needed this for working with Oklab colors.

In the future, double and half precision or integer cube roots might be good additions, although I expect this to cover the most common cases.

I'm happy to make any changes to the code.

author: pmatseykanets
body:
## Issue: <!-- link the issue or issues this PR resolves here -->
<!-- If your PR depends on changes from another pr link them here and describe why they are needed on your solution section. -->
https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/43668
 
## Problem
<!-- Describe the root cause of the issue you are resolving. This may include what behavior is observed and why it is not desirable. If this is a new feature describe why we need this feature and how it will be used. -->

There is a typo in the type declaration
```golang
type OIDCConfig struct {
	// ...
	Scopes             string `json:"scope", norman:"required,notnullable"`
	//                                     ^
	//...
}
```
Tags shouldn't be separated by a comma.

```
struct field tag `json:"scope", norman:"required,notnullable"` not compatible with reflect.StructTag.Get: key:"value" pairs not separated by spacesstructtag[default](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/passes/structtag)
```

And another one
```golang
type ClaimInfo struct {
	// ...
	PreferredUsername string   `json:preferred_username`
	GivenName         string   `json:given_name`
	FamilyName        string   `json:family_name`
	// ...
}
```
Missing double quotes around the field names.

```
struct field tag `json:given_name` not compatible with reflect.StructTag.Get: bad syntax for struct tag valuestructtag[default](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/passes/structtag)
```

## Solution
<!-- Describe what you changed to fix the issue. Relate your changes back to the original issue / feature and explain why this addresses the issue. -->
Remove norman tag from `OIDCConfig.Scopes` field to keep validation intact and add missing double quotes in `ClaimInfo`.

Note [this](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/blob/07b114dd21372f69efdec2d5c5222b696af9eaa0/pkg/auth/providers/oidc/oidc_provider.go#L420-L421) ensures we have at least one scope (`openid`) set.

## Testing
<!-- Note: Confirm if the repro steps in the GitHub issue are valid, if not, please update the issue with accurate repro steps. -->

author: joshj24
body:
The authentication use case was modified so that end-users can now create multiple accounts rather than just one, where each account is represented by a distinct username and password stored in the database. Previously, users were only able to configure one authentication key/account for a single password database. Thus 'username' was added as a variable so that the authentication use case can still keep track of each user's password except associated with their username and userID as well, to be passed in to the Dashboard use case.

The pull request contains the following features: 

- Appropriate files were updated with the 'username' variable and methods were updated to pass in username as a parameter
- Added validate method to validate whether inputted password matches username
- Added functionality for user to switch to the SignUp(SetupAuth) screen
- Added a userID which is an integer associated with each user's username to be passed through to Dashboard use case
- Method was added to generate and store unique salt for each user's derived key to be passed and used in Dashboard use case
- The Swing GUI for the Authentication view was updated to use a .form file for easier designing of the view through IntelliJ's Swing GUI Designer tool
- General code-cleanup and some documentation/javadocs were added to improve documentation and code organization(also removed some unused code such as InMemoryAuthDataAccessObject) 
- Improved the overall look and feel of the views

author: thejaminator
body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the title above. -->

Initial work that allows you to use pydantic classes out of the box, without converting it into a strawberry dataclass type.

Start of https://github.com/strawberry-graphql/strawberry/issues/2181

What works
- Basic usage of just using the pydantic type as an input / output

What doesn't work (Alot of things, don't use this yet)
- Directives
- Strawberry fields
- Resolvers

What is tested so far
- test_basic.py tests.


Two issues I encountered while implementing
- A pydantic type cannot be both an input and output graphql type. Because we are currently overwriting the same `__strawberry_definition__`. When you register it as a input type, and after an output type, that original definition for the input type gets overwritten. https://github.com/strawberry-graphql/strawberry/pull/3268#discussion_r1412893016
- You cannot manually define how to handle a validation error for a pydantic input type. https://github.com/strawberry-graphql/strawberry/pull/3268#discussion_r1412898230 . Maybe instead users should define a custom pydantic [error](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/validators/)?

author: dominiklohmann
body:
These two operators combined allow for replaying a data set in real-time—which is really useful when giving demos.

The `timeshift [--replay-speed <replay-speed>] <field>` operator adjusts a given series of time values $`X_0, ..., X_n`$ to $`X_n' = T + \frac{X_n - X_0}{P}`$, where $`T`$ is the time where the first value arrives at the operator, and $`P`$ is a factor describing the replay speed that defaults to $`1.0`$.

The `delay <field>` operator delays events until the current time is greater or equal to the value of the last entry in the given time series.

For example, the following pipeline replays all Zeek conn logs from the M57 trace used as an example in our documentation at 100x speed.

```
from https://storage.googleapis.com/tenzir-datasets/M57/zeek-all.log.zst read zeek-tsv
| where #schema == "zeek.conn"
| timeshift --replay-speed 100 ts
| delay ts
```

author: jedisct1
body:
The latest AEGIS draft, as well as the IANA TLS registry [1] have been updated to replace `TLS_AEGIS_256_SHA384` with `TLS_AEGIS_256_SHA512`.

This follows the recommendations from [2] for new cipher suites.

[1] https://www.iana.org/assignments/tls-parameters/tls-parameters.xhtml#tls-parameters-4
[2] https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/913.pdf

author: robinmordasiewicz
body:
Optimizes the favicon creation process in our GitHub workflow by introducing a check for changes in the profile picture. Previously, the workflow would run regardless of whether there were any changes, resulting in unnecessary resource consumption and time wastage.

With this change, the workflow will only run when there are changes in the profile picture. This prevents unnecessary runs, saving valuable resources and time. Additionally, the profile picture is now saved in a more appropriate location (docs/img/profile-picture.png) for better organization.

Overall, these changes improve the efficiency of the favicon creation process and enhance the organization of our project's assets.

author: gh0stwalk3r
body:
resolves #2 (first part)
This PR adds CI support for code coverage and mutation testing.

In addition to the requirements, it adds reporting of the code coverage and mutation testing to the PR and the GitHub-Action summary as Markdown. Another difference is that the job `Collect Code Coverage` does not `restore .NET local tools` and instead performs a restore of the NuGet packages. Coverlet is installed as a project reference and not as a tool therefore the normal NuGet package restore is sufficient.
